taxonomyNote: NatureServe: Ovis aries is the domestic form of O. gmelini; Grubb included O. orientalis, O. musimon and O. ophion (now feral) in O. aries.
fieldMarks: Head-body 1,200-1,800 mm, shoulder 650-1,270 mm; ewes two-thirds to three-quarters the size of rams
Coloration from milky white to dark brown and black; wool, horns and external ears vary by breed
Vertical cleft in a narrow, short-haired snout
Domestic-derived; goats can be told from sheep by their short, upward-pointing tails (Pacific Science review of feral goats)
behavior: Strong flocking instinct, groups up to 1,000 or more, with dominance hierarchies
Distressed when separated, often calling and pawing the ground
Grazers that alternate feeding and rumination
habitat: Extremely versatile: desert, grassland, chaparral, forest and mountain.
range: Domestic sheep are established worldwide as introduced animals. DLNR lists feral sheep and mouflon-feral hybrid sheep on Hawaii Island (Mauna Kea); NatureServe records Ovis aries in Wyoming and Hawaii.

lookalikes.name: Mouflon
lookalikes.howToTell: European mouflon has a reddish-brown summer coat with whitish saddle patch and rams' helix horns; hybrids with feral sheep occur on Mauna Kea.
